source_metadata.title: Three- Versus Two-Drug Therapy for Patients With Newly Diagnosed Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension
source_metadata.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

large_source_manifest.source_type: randomized phase 3b clinical trial with protocol/SAP supplement
large_source_manifest.supplement_scope: Supplementary methods, 5 supplementary figures, 9 supplementary result tables, final protocol, statistical analysis plan, post-hoc statistical analysis plan, and administrative appendices.
large_source_manifest.coverage_decision: Primary article fully mapped. Supplementary trial-results tables/figures and load-bearing protocol/SAP methods were extracted. Administrative investigator/committee lists, sponsor contacts, signatures, routine operational procedures, and protocol boilerplate were not atomized because they do not materially alter trial evidence interpretation.
omissions_and_reasons: Administrative investigator/committee rosters: provenance/governance infrastructure, not independently useful evidence claims for the trial result.
Sponsor contact/signature pages and routine operational procedures: non-evidentiary administrative content.
Protocol sections that repeat the same objective, intervention, endpoint, or statistical rule already represented by a more specific atom were not duplicated.
The complete long-tail of protocol exclusion criteria was not atomized individually; key criteria affecting clinical population definition and external validity were retained.

notes: Repeated primary/supplement statements were represented once unless the supplement added a distinct sensitivity, analysis-set, dosing, or tolerability assertion.
Safety-set denominators differ by analysis definition; atoms preserve the denominators reported for each row rather than forcing one common denominator.

schema_gaps: The current LiteratureAtom schema has no dedicated field for trial-registration identifiers, source-document identity, multiplicity hierarchy, or visual-representation metadata; these are preserved in tags, canonical statements, provenance, and the separate validation manifest.

Adverse-event atoms can store one primary quantitative estimate plus arm observations, but do not natively encode comparative risk differences/ratios unless those are reported or calculated as separate atoms.
extraction_limitations: No unreported study detail was inferred or added.
All long-term disease-progression and mortality signals are labeled exploratory/post hoc where the source indicates this.
The supplement is substantially larger than the article; semantic batching was used to preserve trial-relevant protocol/SAP content without treating administrative text as evidence.
